id-photo.q1: What size is a passport photo?
id-photo.a1: A US passport photo is 2 × 2 inches (51 × 51 mm) with the head 1 to 1 3/8 inches (25–35 mm) from chin to top of head. The UK, Japan, Korea, Taiwan and most of Europe use 35 × 45 mm; China uses 33 × 48 mm. Pick the size and line the head up with the guides.
id-photo.q2: Can I change the background of a passport photo?
id-photo.a2: Usually not. The US, UK, Korea, China and Taiwan reject passport photos whose background was cut out or edited with software. For those sizes the tool keeps your original background and only crops: take the photo against a plain white wall. Background replacement is for résumés, school and work IDs and forms that accept it.
id-photo.q3: How do I print passport photos at the right size?
id-photo.a3: Download the print sheet: a 4 × 6 in JPEG at 300 DPI, or an A4 or Letter PDF. Print it at 100 % (actual size), not "fit to page", on photo paper, or order a 4 × 6 print at a photo lab, then cut along the thin lines.
id-photo.a4: No. Cropping happens in the page. When you replace the background, the background-removal model downloads once and runs on your device; the photo never leaves it.
id-photo.q5: How do I get a photo under a file size limit?
id-photo.a5: Online forms often ask for a pixel size and a maximum file size, such as 600 × 600 px under 240 KB. Enter both before you download: the tool lowers the JPEG quality first and only shrinks the picture if it still does not fit.

id-photo.lead: Make an ID photo in three steps.
id-photo.s1t: Choose a photo and a size
id-photo.s1b: Pick a front-facing photo in even light, then the passport, visa or ID size you need.
id-photo.s2b: Drag and zoom until the top of the head touches the top line and the chin sits in the band.
id-photo.s3b: Download the photo for an online form, or a 4 × 6 or A4 sheet to print at actual size.
